A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main text, figures, tables, equations and supplementary Sections 6–8 support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V4 reports original synthetic and real-data pose-estimation experiments, including accuracy, runtime, robustness and ablation results.

after.justification: V5 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and the supplementary material.

M1.justification: The affine and mean-point solvers, delta perturbations, early non-minimal refitting, filtering and refinement procedures in Sections 3.1–3.2 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both retain the same synthetic scenarios and PhotoTourism, Cambridge Landmarks, Aachen Day-Night v1.1 and ETH3D experiments. No dataset, task or evaluation population is added or removed.

E2.justification: The 5pt+P3P and 4p3v(HC) comparisons and the oracle comparison with Nistér and Schaffalitzky [37] are retained. V5's abbreviated Table 3 does not remove comparators from the full comparison in Table 2.

E3.justification: Feature extraction, matching, sampling, RANSAC settings, thresholds and pose-error metrics are unchanged. V5 Table 3 repeats results under Table 2's existing protocol.

E4.justification: The geometry/noise tests, delta and refinement ablations, threshold and outlier sensitivity analyses, and oracle comparison are retained. Section 8.6 moves across pages but contains no new analysis.

E5.justification: Boxplot quantiles, median summaries and Gaussian-fit reporting are unchanged. There are no added or revised seed, repeated-run, confidence-interval or significance-test disclosures.

E6.justification: All six original tables retain their numerical entries, and the plotted results and qualitative findings are unchanged. V5 Table 3 repeats nine rows from retained Table 2, adding no new outcomes.

T1.justification: Lemma 1 and its proof in Section 6.1, the mean-point constraint derivation in Section 6.2, and Equations 1–4 are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same solver contributions, implementation-simplicity claims and claims about accuracy and robustness on real data.

C2.justification: The explanations of approximation error, scene dependence and the role of refitting are retained, as are the limitations concerning two-view performance and competing solvers.

D1.justification: Section 1 adds separate Zenodo DOI links for the source code and experimental data alongside the existing GitHub link. Implementation details and experimental parameters otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 60 works and retain the same research positioning, including the discussion of [37] in Section 8.6. Bibliographic differences concern page back-references.

P1.justification: The availability statement is expanded, and table cross-references and version-header text change. The section hierarchy and scientific prose remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: V5 adds a color-highlighted Table 3 containing nine rows from Table 2. Existing figures and tables shift with reflow, and subsequent tables are renumbered; all 19 figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The added code and data archive identifiers improve reproducibility documentation beyond v4's GitHub-only availability statement. The extra summary table introduces some redundancy, while the scientific evidence remains unchanged, making the overall gain limited.
